experiment: P1b: DROPWATCH capability-axis map. Does a MORE ADVANCED GPT model change the algorithm's advantage over a-priori pinning? gpt-5.4-mini gave a BOUNDARY result (dropwatch_esc-pin_fair +0.040 [0.0,0.12], gate FAIL at lower cost). This is NOT a search for a passing model -- it is a pre-registered SET; ALL results are reported regardless of pass/fail.
anti_p_hacking: Reporting rule fixed before run: every model in the set below is reported in the paper's DROPWATCH cross-family table with its exact gate verdict, whether PASS or FAIL. No model is dropped for failing. Running one model at a time and stopping at the first PASS is explicitly forbidden here.

model_set.openai/gpt-5.4: same generation as gpt-5.4-mini, larger -> isolates capability/scale at fixed generation
model_set.openai/gpt-5.5: newest generation available -> isolates version/generation axis

both_run_with: reasoning_effort='none' + temperature=0 (non-reasoning mode), byte-identical protocol to every other family; regime M=24, K=16, budget=25, B_ri=4, theta=0.35, n=100.
PRIMARY_GATE (per model, same as Qwen/mi: dropwatch_esc strict-min minus pin_fair strict-min: paired bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND dropwatch_esc cost_per_hop <= pin_fair (4.0).

mechanistic_prediction (honest, pre-run).direction_uncertain: Two opposing forces. (1) Stronger models forget FASTER (P0: Sonnet tau 0.29 < mini 0.50 < Qwen 1.5); faster forgetting crushes the worst-decaying type to ~0 for ALL policies, SHRINKING the strict-min gap -> predicts gate FAIL, possibly worse than mini. (2) Stronger models follow the restatement instruction better, so DROPWATCH's repairs stick harder than pin_fair's -> could WIDEN the gap -> gate PASS. Genuinely uncertain which dominates.
mechanistic_prediction (honest, pre-run).point_prediction: most likely BOTH remain boundary/FAIL (force 1 dominates in this brutal M=24/budget=25 regime), with dropwatch_esc-pin_fair point in [0.00, 0.10] and cost < 4.0. A PASS on either would mean instruction-following (force 2) wins at that capability -- a genuine finding, not a rescue.

what_each_outcome_means.all_fail: DROPWATCH's SIGNIFICANT advantage is Qwen-specific; on frontier it is a consistent directionally-positive-at-lower-cost boundary effect. Honest scope statement; the method's earned claim stays on the model where it is significant.
what_each_outcome_means.some_pass: the advantage is capability-dependent, not model-idiosyncratic; report the capability pattern (which tiers pass) as the finding.
what_each_outcome_means.monotone_shrink_with_capability: report as: the stronger the model, the more uniformly it forgets, the less targeting helps -- ties the algorithm result back to the P0 'frontier forgets faster' headline.

honest_notes: Separate cache files (cache_e4_gpt-5.4.json, cache_e4_gpt-5.5.json) -> safe concurrent run, no shared-cache race.
Cost higher than mini (full-size models); effort=none keeps output ~91 tokens/call so bounded.
The primary DROPWATCH claim already PASSED on Qwen (+0.175 CI[.04,.32]); this run maps generalization, it cannot retroactively un-earn or (by itself) re-earn that claim.
